PullRequest.Title: chat-lib: let NES embedders supply language context and workspace services
PullRequest.Body:
`createNESProvider` hardcodes `NullLanguageContextProviderService` and `NullWorkspaceService`, so outside VS Code `XtabProvider.getLanguageContext` never finds the active document or a context provider, even with `languageContext.enabled` on.

This adds optional `languageContextProvider` and `workspaceService` to `INESProviderOptions`, following the existing `languageDiagnosticsService` option and the inline completions provider's `languageContextProvider`. Omitting them keeps today's behavior. Note that a supplied `workspaceService` is also what cross-file edits use to open their target document.

Motivation: the Copilot language server wants to pass declarations from the JetBrains code model (PSI) into NES prompts.

**Testing:** a new `nesProvider.spec.ts` case checks that a snippet from an embedder-supplied provider reaches the `/chat/completions` prompt; it fails without this change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create an NES provider and query capabilities, with either omitted or supplied service hooks.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setupServices registers supplied instances or the same null-service descriptors as before. XtabProvider construction only stores the two service references; it does not enumerate documents or request context. Capability queries await existing model selection and any necessary authentication/model discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and parse the /models response after obtaining authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful fetch for a cold token, with concurrent requests coalesced by TaskSingler using the token string. Warm successful loads return without fetching; failed loads are not recorded as successful.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical model-discovery path, token cache, and coalescing before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required when model selection needs discovery; no language-context collection is performed by capability queries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One service registration per option per provider instance; model discovery is per authentication token, not per document or registered language-context provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Service registration is synchronous constant-count work. Model discovery retains existing per-token coalescing; no additional jobs or concurrency are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model responses are cached for the current token and in-flight loads are coalesced by token. The added hooks do not alter cache keys, negative-cache behavior, or service construction scheduling. Omitting both options preserves the previous descriptors exactly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both production hunks, the service builder, NESProvider constructor, XtabProvider constructor, and model-discovery implementation were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Construction and internal resource ownership of an embedder-supplied service are outside this repository; no extra constructor work is required by these hooks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: optional dependency injection does not itself introduce eager boundary work, repeat initialization, or add lifecycle listeners.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request a next edit with embedder-supplied language context enabled, including repeated requests and cancellation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An uncached request finds the active TextDocument, checks matching NES providers, and awaits context collection raced against cancellation and the remaining debounce budget. Prompt construction follows, then the remaining debounce and the streaming completion request. DelaySession subtracts elapsed collection time, so context collection does not add a second full debounce. With context disabled, collection is skipped unless recording explicitly requests it; recording-only collection is not awaited for prompting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delegate to the supplied getContextItems async iterable and getContextItemsOnTimeout. The external service may use IPC or a host code model, but its implementation is not present here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getContextItems invocation and one timeout-item lookup per eligible fresh prompt attempt; items are consumed sequentially. Matching providers are checked as a group rather than invoked by a new library-side fan-out loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The empty NullWorkspaceService document list normally stopped this path before invoking context providers. Supplying both hooks intentionally enables the existing context pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Context-enabled prompting waits within the remaining debounce race; recording-only collection is off the prompt critical path. Cancellation is forwarded to the service.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format selected snippets into the existing prompt, then use the existing chat-request serialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Snippet inclusion is limited by the configured token budget; the final prompt also has the existing 120,000-character guard. No new per-snippet serialization boundary is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same formatter, budgets, and final guard existed, but the library's null services supplied no language-context snippets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prompt assembly precedes the completion request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing streaming chat completion request using endpoint.makeChatRequest2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One completion request per fresh prompt attempt, subject to existing cancellation, retry, and cursor-prediction paths. No extra completion request is created for each context item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was already made without the optional context snippets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before an uncached suggestion can arrive.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D open text documents for the active-document lookup, C yielded context items and their URI lists, and the configured snippet token budget. One async context-collection invocation per fresh prompt attempt, not one network request per snippet or provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A context stream is consumed sequentially, with URI checks grouped within each snippet and resolved by the no-op ignore service. Existing request reuse and cancellation remain unchanged. Internal provider parallelism and cancellation cooperation belong to the supplied implementation; the diff adds no fan-out scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: NextEditProvider checks the edit cache before fetching and joins compatible pending regular or speculative requests, avoiding duplicate context collection on those paths. No new library-level context-result cache is added; external provider caching is unspecified. NullIgnoreService remains installed, so snippet ignore checks do not perform filesystem or network I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the traced gate, remaining-debounce timeout, request reuse, token budgeting, and unchanged completion count. No concrete external-provider IPC or network implementation is available.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host provider latency, snippet volume, cache behavior, and cancellation responsiveness cannot be measured or inferred from the new API or fixed-size test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance bug: the new work is the explicitly enabled feature and uses the existing timeout, cancellation, budgeting, and request-reuse path. Possible weaknesses in that existing pipeline do not establish a diff-introduced regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve a cross-file cursor prediction into an edit using the supplied workspace service.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an initial completion yields no usable edits, an enabled predictor may make a prediction request. For a different-file OnlyWithEdit prediction, the existing handler awaits opening the target document, checks cancellation and intervening typing, creates its snapshot, and makes a follow-up edit attempt. The RetryState guard prevents recursive cursor-jump prediction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the next cursor position through endpoint.makeChatRequest2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cursor-prediction request in this chain because retrying edit attempts skip further cursor prediction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same optional prediction request could already run with null workspace services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes after the first no-edit response and before the target can be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the workspace service to open one predicted target document; an embedder may satisfy this from memory or perform filesystem/IPC access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One openTextDocument call per eligible cross-file prediction. There is no workspace-wide file enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The call site already existed, but NullWorkspaceService had no documents and rejected immediately. Injection permits a real host-backed open to succeed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before reading the target snapshot and requesting the follow-up edit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request an edit for the successfully resolved target document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One follow-up edit attempt per cursor-jump chain, apart from the existing guarded model-not-found fallback; not a request per file in the workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The handler and follow-up implementation existed, but the library's empty workspace service prevented successful target resolution and this follow-up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to obtain the cross-file edit; it is serialized after target opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one predicted target and one target-document open per cursor-jump chain, rather than one open per workspace file. Snapshot work scales with target file size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial completion, optional prediction, target opening, and target follow-up are sequential for one chain. Existing compatible-request joining is preserved. No new per-file parallelism or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workspace service owns document-open caching. Existing edit-cache hits can avoid the prediction/open/follow-up chain when the target is open and matches its cached snapshot; invalid targets fall back to a fresh request. The PR does not change those checks or keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: target opening, snapshot creation, follow-up, and the retry guard were read directly, along with cache validation and pending-request reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold target-open latency and file sizes depend on the embedding workspace. No concrete implementation or timings accompany the hook.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: these bounded operations are necessary to deliver the newly supported cross-file result, and no redundant opens, unbounded retries, or multiplied boundary calls are introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the added embedder-language-context facade test.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Read one reply fixture, construct a provider with one in-memory document and one yielded snippet, request an edit through a fake fetcher, dispose the provider, and inspect the captured prompt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixture read for the added test invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This additional test and its fixture read did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited during test setup only; not on any product request path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the captured fake completion request for the snippet assertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for a bounded test prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the provider request and disposal in the test.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed-size document, one snippet, and the fixed reply fixture in one new test case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One sequential test workflow; the fake context iterator yields one item without external work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The test uses fresh in-memory services and a fake fetcher with fixed responses. It adds no product cache and no live network access.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete added test and its fake fetcher were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful scaling uncertainty: the test data is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: only bounded additional test work is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete two-file inventory and every diff page against base 306a2166454856f58ea7e1b75c7c70b9cac4b99e. Traced startup/model discovery, optional language-context collection and budgeting, request caching/coalescing, cross-file prediction/open/follow-up, and the added test. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings or concrete performance-regression fixes were identified. External embedder implementations remain outside the available evidence.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
